newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes $7 down, catches up with Brent.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes $7 down, catches up with Brent.

text.p: IPE gas oil failed to bounce back after opening sharply lower on Friday in a catch-up with a late Thursday slump on Brent.
Nov gas oil closed $7 lower at $212 a tonne, 75 cents above the session low, having started the day's trading $5 down at $214.
"Gas oil came in very weak and has not shown any signs of filling the gap up to yesterday's levels," said one IPE floor trader.
The Dec gas oil/Brent crack spread slipped to $5.07 a barrel, 23 cents down on Thursday's close.

The absence of many players due to a Roman Catholic holiday in Austria, Belgium, France, Italy, Spain and parts of Germany depleted trading volumes on both the physical and futures markets, dealers said.
Dec Brent was trading five cents up at $22.77 a barrel at 1749 GMT.
The contract had briefly dipped into the red to touch a low of $22.50 as pressure built on NYMEX crude.
Comments by U.S. ambassador to the U.N. Madeleine Albright that Iraq was making "outrageous demands" on how to implement the food-for-oil deal helped the market retrace losses, traders said.
But the news failed to trigger a sharp fall and traders said there was still room for the market to move down.
"There are still a lot of longs out there," said Charles Gray of Prudential Bache Futures in his daily report.

A statement on Thursday from the American Petroleum Institute (API) president Charles DiBona that there was ample winter heating oil inventories was still exerting pressure on the market, dealers said.
